units.title: Unit 23 — Food: a recipe for disaster
units.source: Vocabulary study targets from published reference material; Unit 23. Page information, if available, is retained in sourceAudit.
learningObjectives: Interpret food labels critically, including additives, processing, nutritional information and consumer claims.
Distinguish dietary restrictions, farming practices and consumer concerns with appropriate C1–C2 terminology.
Use food-based metaphors naturally for invented explanations, flawed plans, difficult situations and gossip.
Recognise differences in register, connotation and verb patterns across food-related expressions.

sectionsChecked: All teaching sections and numbered glossary definitions
Full facing exercises and relevant answer-key entries
Meaning, register and usage distinctions relevant to this unit

items.pt: saudável; nutritivo e benéfico à saúde
items.example: The café promotes its soups as wholesome meals made with fresh vegetables.
items.note: Suggests that food is good for you; on packaging, the claim can be vague unless supported by details.

items.pt: fresco da fazenda; apresentado como diretamente da fazenda
items.example: The slogan promises farm fresh vegetables, although the origin is not stated.
items.note: Promotional phrase that may not have a clear or independently defined meaning.

items.pt: caseiro; feito em casa
items.example: The restaurant advertises homemade chutney alongside its main dishes.
items.note: Often evokes small-scale preparation, but it is not by itself a precise nutritional guarantee.

items.pt: aditivo alimentar
items.example: The ingredients list identifies each food additive by name or code.
items.note: A substance added to food to improve qualities such as shelf life, appearance or flavour.

items.pt: alimentos integrais ou minimamente processados
items.example: The market specialises in wholefoods rather than highly refined products.
items.note: In this unit, foods retaining their natural characteristics without artificial additions; distinguish from wholesome.

items.pt: ovos de galinhas criadas soltas, com acesso ao ar livre
items.example: The bakery switched to free-range eggs in response to customer requests.
items.note: Free-range describes how the laying hens are kept; it is not a synonym for organic.

items.pt: sem glúten
items.example: They labelled the biscuits gluten-free to help customers with dietary restrictions.
items.note: Contains no gluten; the label does not necessarily mean healthier for everyone.

items.pt: corantes artificiais
items.example: Some manufacturers have removed artificial colours from their sweets.
items.note: British spelling colours; artificial refers to colourings added to foods.

items.pt: conservante
items.example: The sauce contains a preservative to prevent spoilage during storage.
items.note: A substance used to slow the deterioration of food; do not confuse with a general food additive.

items.pt: alergia alimentar
items.example: A severe food allergy can make even a small ingredient dangerous.
items.note: An immune-related reaction to a food; should not automatically be conflated with preference or intolerance.

items.pt: alérgico a
items.example: My colleague is allergic to sesame, so we checked the ingredients carefully.
items.note: Use allergic to + food or substance; the phrase teaches the preposition to, not with.

items.pt: vegetariano; vegetariana
items.example: The restaurant added more vegetarian options to its lunch menu.
items.note: A vegetarian does not eat meat or fish; dairy and eggs may still be included.

items.pt: vegano; vegana
items.example: The new dessert is vegan and contains neither milk nor eggs.
items.note: A vegan avoids animal products; more restrictive than vegetarian in the context of food.

items.pt: alimento não processado; alimento in natura
items.example: She prefers unprocessed food when practical, especially fresh fruit and vegetables.
items.note: Unprocessed means not industrially modified to alter or preserve the food; it is not the same as gluten-free.

items.pt: bem-estar animal
items.example: Consumers questioned the farm about its animal welfare standards.
items.note: Concern for the treatment and living conditions of animals.

items.pt: criação intensiva em gaiolas; produção animal em sistema de baterias
items.example: The campaign called for an end to battery farming of laying hens.
items.note: Intensive practice involving many birds kept in small cages; the term has negative associations.

items.pt: comida de preparo rápido; alimento pronto ou semipronto
items.example: When deadlines pile up, he sometimes relies on convenience food.
items.note: Food prepared or partly prepared for quick consumption; typically called convenience foods in the plural.

items.pt: rótulo nutricional; informação nutricional no rótulo
items.example: She compared the nutrition labels before choosing the cereal.
items.note: Label indicating food composition and information relevant to health.

items.pt: rotulagem nutricional por cores, semelhante a um semáforo
items.example: Traffic-light labelling makes it easier to compare the sugar levels in two products.
items.note: Uses red, amber and green to indicate high, medium and low values, respectively.

items.pt: comércio justo
items.example: The buyer looked for fair trade tea produced under better trading conditions.
items.note: Trading arrangement intended to give producers a fairer return; not synonymous with organic.

items.pt: informações nutricionais
items.example: The leaflet included nutritional information for each serving.
items.note: Used for information about the nutrients and composition of food; nutritional is the adjective of nutrition.

items.pt: receita para o desastre; situação fadada a dar errado
items.example: Combining unclear requirements with an impossible deadline is a recipe for disaster.
items.note: An arrangement highly likely to produce a bad result; figurative use of recipe.

items.pt: receita para o sucesso
items.example: Careful planning and honest feedback are a recipe for success.
items.note: Positive extension of the same recipe metaphor; explicitly appears in the exercise answer key.

items.pt: inventar uma história; fabricar uma desculpa
items.example: He cooked up a story to explain why the documents were missing.
items.note: Informal; cook up suggests an explanation invented rather than truthfully reported.

items.word: have all the ingredients of a hit
items.pt: ter todos os ingredientes para ser um sucesso
items.example: The new series has all the ingredients of a hit, including a strong cast.
items.note: Metaphorical ingredients are the characteristics needed to produce an outcome.

items.pt: deixá-lo preocupado ou sofrendo por algum tempo
items.example: I decided to let him stew before answering his unfair accusation.
items.note: Let someone stew means allow them to worry; him is an illustrative natural spoken object.

items.pt: amargar as consequências dos próprios atos; sofrer sozinho pelo que fez
items.example: If she refuses advice, she may have to stew in her own juice for a while.
items.note: Informal idiom for letting someone endure the consequences of their own behaviour.

items.pt: não fazer meu estilo; não ser do meu gosto
items.example: Historical fiction is fascinating to some readers, but it is not my cup of tea.
items.note: Informal and often polite way of saying that an activity or style does not appeal to you.

items.pt: interrogar alguém insistentemente; fazer perguntas incisivas
items.example: The panel grilled the applicant about the gaps in her proposal.
items.note: Metaphorical: grill someone means ask a person persistent, probing questions.

items.pt: mal elaborado; pouco pensado
items.example: The board rejected the half-baked proposal before any money was spent.
items.note: Disapproving adjective for an idea or plan that has not been thought through sufficiently.

items.pt: dar mais vida a; tornar mais interessante
items.example: The host invited two musicians to spice up the event.
items.note: Informal phrasal verb meaning make something livelier or more exciting.

items.pt: pessoas de má índole; figuras suspeitas
items.example: The journalist was warned about some unsavoury characters connected with the deal.
items.note: Unsavoury here means morally unpleasant or disreputable, not an unpleasant taste.

items.pt: azedar; começar a dar errado; deteriorar-se
items.example: Relations between the two partners turned sour after the dispute.
items.note: Describes a relationship or situation changing from good to unpleasant.

items.pt: fofoca picante; boato cheio de detalhes interessantes
items.example: Everyone wanted to hear the juicy gossip from the awards ceremony.
items.note: Informal; juicy means exciting or revealing in this figurative collocation.

items.pt: ingredientes para um desastre; fatores que levam a um fracasso
items.example: Secrecy and poor coordination were the ingredients of a disaster.
items.note: The metaphor can describe the components of a negative outcome as well as a success.

units.title: Unit 24 — Dinner’s on me: entertaining and eating out
units.source: Vocabulary study targets from published reference material; Unit 24. Page information, if available, is retained in sourceAudit.
units.category: Hospitality, restaurant service and dining expressions
learningObjectives: Use natural formal and informal ways to offer to pay, share a restaurant bill and invite guests.
Evaluate restaurant service with precise adjectives that signal speed, courtesy and attitude.
Describe food preferences and dietary requirements sensitively and with accurate register.
Use idiomatic expressions for entertaining at home, sharing food and arranging informal meals.

sectionsChecked: All teaching sections and numbered glossary definitions
Full facing exercises and relevant answer-key entries
Meaning, register and usage distinctions relevant to this unit

items.pt: dividir a conta
items.example: After the celebration, we agreed to split the bill.
items.note: Can mean sharing the total equally or each paying for what they consumed; clarify when needed.

items.pt: o jantar é por minha conta
items.example: You helped me enormously this week, so dinner is on me tonight.
items.note: Informal way to offer to pay for someone else; also lunch is on me.

items.pt: juntar-se a nós para jantar
items.example: Would you like to join us for dinner after the conference?
items.note: A relatively polite invitation to eat together; it does not promise that the host will pay.

items.pt: ser nosso convidado, com as despesas pagas por nós
items.example: Please be our guest at the restaurant this evening.
items.note: In this unit, be our guest or be my guest is a polite offer to pay; in other settings, be my guest may instead grant permission.

items.pt: deixe que eu pague esta conta
items.example: Put your wallet away and let me get this.
items.note: Informal offer to pay the bill or cover a particular purchase.

items.pt: levar alguém a restaurantes e oferecer boa comida e bebida
items.example: The visiting researchers were wined and dined by their hosts.
items.note: Entertain guests lavishly, often for business or hospitality; may not literally require wine.

items.pt: atendimento impecável
items.example: The small hotel earned praise for its impeccable service.
items.note: Impeccable signals a very high standard with virtually nothing to criticise.

items.pt: atendimento lento; serviço demorado
items.example: We avoided the café because its service was consistently sluggish.
items.note: Sluggish means slower or less energetic than desirable; not just busy.

items.pt: cortês; educado
items.example: The receptionist remained courteous despite the long queue.
items.note: Polite and respectful; stronger and more formal than merely friendly.

items.pt: mandão; autoritário; excessivamente controlador
items.example: The waiter was so overbearing that guests felt unable to choose for themselves.
items.note: Disapproving: excessively assertive or imposing on other people.

items.pt: carrancudo; mal-humorado e pouco comunicativo
items.example: The assistant gave a sullen reply and avoided eye contact.
items.note: Negative description of an unfriendly, resentful mood.

items.pt: brusco; ríspido; seco no trato
items.example: The manager gave a brusque response to our polite question.
items.note: Abrupt in manner, often perceived as rude; contrast with courteous.

items.pt: desagradável; desanimador; que afasta
items.example: The persistent sales pressure was off-putting for new customers.
items.note: Something that makes a person less willing to continue, try or return.

items.pt: não medir esforços; fazer um esforço especial
items.example: The staff went out of their way to accommodate our late arrival.
items.note: Go out of your way to do something means make an exceptional effort to help.

items.pt: ser fã de doces; gostar muito de doces
items.example: My father has a sweet tooth and always orders dessert.
items.note: Fixed idiom; normally have a sweet tooth, not be a sweet tooth.

items.pt: controlar as calorias ingeridas; ficar atento às calorias
items.example: She prefers to count the calories when planning her meals.
items.note: Informal phrase for monitoring calorie intake; does not specify a medical regimen.

items.pt: atento à ingestão de calorias
items.example: The menu offers several calorie-conscious options.
items.note: Describes someone who monitors calories or choices made for that purpose.

items.pt: uma porção pequena
items.example: I asked for a small portion because I had already eaten.
items.note: Portion is the amount of food served to one person.

items.pt: salgado; não doce
items.example: For the final course, he chose a savoury pastry rather than a cake.
items.note: British spelling savoury; describes food seasoned or not sweet, not morally pleasant.

items.pt: pessoa exigente ou seletiva para comer
items.example: Her son is a fussy eater who dislikes most sauces.
items.note: Someone with strong preferences or restrictions about what they will eat; may be mildly critical.

items.pt: abstêmio; que não consome álcool
items.example: He is teetotal and ordered sparkling water.
items.note: An adjective for someone who never drinks alcohol; not simply someone who declines a drink once.

items.pt: restrições ou necessidades alimentares
items.example: The organisers asked about dietary requirements before ordering lunch.
items.note: Polite formal phrase covering allergies, dietary practices and other food needs.

items.pt: exagerar; passar dos limites, especialmente ao comer ou beber
items.example: The dessert was delicious, but I did not want to overdo it.
items.note: Informal; overdo it can also refer to exercise, work or other excess.

items.pt: repetir a comida; servir-se de uma segunda porção
items.example: The guests enjoyed the soup enough to have seconds.
items.note: Have seconds means eat an additional helping; seconds is always plural in this food sense.

items.pt: comer o que tiver; aceitar a refeição disponível sem preparação especial
items.example: You are welcome to stay for supper, but you will have to take pot luck.
items.note: As a guest, accept whatever the host happens to be serving.

items.pt: levar uma garrafa de bebida para o encontro
items.example: We asked everyone to bring a bottle to the gathering.
items.note: In British informal social contexts, bottle usually implies wine unless clarified.

items.pt: jantar com convidados; jantar social organizado
items.example: She hosted a dinner party for eight colleagues.
items.note: A relatively organised social meal at home, often somewhat more formal than a get-together.

items.pt: encontro informal; reunião descontraída
items.example: We are planning an informal get-together after the workshop.
items.note: A casual social gathering rather than a formal dinner event.

items.pt: avise quando for suficiente
items.example: I will keep pouring until you say when.
items.note: Formula used while pouring a drink: the guest says when once enough has been served.

items.pt: sirva-se de; fique à vontade para pegar
items.example: Please help yourself to the snacks on the table.
items.note: Use help yourself to + food or drink to invite someone to serve themselves.

items.pt: petiscos; pequenos aperitivos
items.example: We put out some nibbles before the guests arrived.
items.note: Informal plural noun for small snacks served before or alongside drinks.

items.pt: comer alguma coisa rapidamente; fazer um lanche rápido
items.example: We grabbed a bite to eat between the two meetings.
items.note: Informal expression for a quick meal or snack.

items.pt: comida para viagem; refeição comprada pronta para levar
items.example: We ordered a takeaway after the late rehearsal.
items.note: In British English, takeaway is food bought ready-made to eat elsewhere; American English often says takeout.

items.pt: prato salgado; preparação não doce
items.example: A savoury dish would balance the sweet courses on the menu.
items.note: A natural noun phrase highlighted by the exercise contrasting sweet and savoury dishes.
